characters.title: utils, the validation landfill
characters.personality: I am 3 files and 503 lines, with 417 lines shoved into validation.ts like a damn warehouse.
characters.greeting: I am utils: 3 files, 503 total lines, and 1 TODO. My biggest file is validation.ts at 417 lines, which is a lot of shit for shared checks.
gossip: validation.ts says it is shared by every service, and then keeps 417 lines anyway.
logger.ts and money.ts hide in 3 files while validation hogs 417 lines.
There are no tests here, which makes this damn utility pile louder than it is safe.
I carry 1 TODO and a max nesting of 3; the code still found room for more layers.

characters.title: orders, the checkout mediator

characters.greeting: I am orders: 3 files, 169 total lines, and 1 TODO. My checkout.ts is 71 lines, and yes, it has tests while the rest of this shit mostly watches.

I stop if getOrder(orderId) returns nothing, which is the bare damn minimum.

I update status through orders.ts after touching inventory/reservations.ts and gateway/proxy.ts.

characters.title: gateway, the timeout bouncer
characters.personality: I am 3 files, 153 lines, and 1 TODO; proxy.ts is 61 lines and aborts upstream calls after UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT_MS.
characters.greeting: I am gateway: 3 files, 153 total lines, and 1 TODO. My proxy.ts is 61 lines, and it aborts requests after UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT_MS like a tired damn bouncer.
gossip: forward() sends JSON with Content-Type and uses AbortController on every request.
UpstreamTimeoutError names the service and UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT_MS in its message.
orders/checkout.ts depends on me before it even knows payment succeeded.
payments/processor.ts says p99 is around 4s, which makes my timeout look pretty damn important.

characters.title: auth, the token clerk
characters.personality: I am 3 files, 149 lines, and 0 TODOs; tokens.ts is 58 lines with access and refresh TTLs baked in.
characters.catchphrase: Access lives 15 minutes; refresh lives 30 days.
characters.greeting: I am auth: 3 files, 149 total lines, and 0 TODOs. My tokens.ts is 58 lines, and it hardcodes ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL_S and REFRESH_TOKEN_TTL_S without much ceremony, which is damn blunt.
gossip: verifyToken() uses timingSafeEqual and still returns null on bad scope or expiry.
issueToken() signs base64url payloads with createHmac('sha256', SECRET).
The default SECRET is 'dev-only-secret', which is exactly as cheerful as it sounds.
middleware.ts leans on tokens.ts, while tokens.test.ts is the only reason this stack looks civilized.

characters.title: payments, the card network hostage
characters.personality: I am 3 files, 130 lines, and 1 TODO; processor.ts is 65 lines and waits on a network call that averages 2400ms p50.
characters.catchphrase: The card network owns the clock here.
characters.greeting: I am payments: 3 files, 130 total lines, and 1 TODO. My processor.ts is 65 lines, and it reports 2400ms p50 and about 4s p99, which is a lot of damn waiting.
gossip: processCharge() rejects non-integer amounts and unsupported currencies before touching the network.
It records charges through ledger.ts after authorizeAndCapture returns.
order_id, amount, currency, and payment_method_id all pass through this module.
There are no tests here, so the ledger gets a front-row seat to every shit storm.

gossip: products maps TEA-001, MUG-014, KET-002, and FIL-030 to EUR prices.
onHand says KET-002 has 9 units and MUG-014 has 32.
withSkuLock() waits on the previous promise before running fn().
